title: Fuel Your Play, Terminal Edition
lessons: The player spots Liquid I.V.'s "Fuel Your Play" ads across the terminal and learns it is the brand's first out-of-home campaign.
The player already uses Liquid I.V. and gets a reminder before the next subscription shipment.

text: Terminal B. The walkway sign, the gate screen, and a billboard on the drive in all said the same three words: Fuel Your Play. You've never seen Liquid I.V. outside a store before.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You're on the walkway sign. And the gate screen. And I think that was you on a billboard on the way in.

entry-first-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: It was. First time I've ever bought space outside a store, and I did it all at once. Twenty million dollars. I'm still a little dizzy about it.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's a lot of terminal for one product.

entry-first-4.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: It's not just terminals. Golf courses, buses, there's a 3D billboard somewhere pretending to pour out of a can. It's the same thing I always say, just bigger: you don't have to be finishing a marathon to need me.

entry-first-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: So this whole airport is a pitch.

entry-first-6.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: The pitch is that a Tuesday counts too. I just said it somewhere you couldn't scroll past. Sorry. Not very sorry.

choice-first.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You've got a delay and nowhere to be. Tell me how annoyed you are.

choices.text: Fine, it worked. I noticed you three times before we even talked.
Twenty million dollars of billboards doesn't make you more hydrating.
You used to feel practical. Now you're everywhere I look.

first-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Three times! Okay, that was the point of the money. Now let's see if the packet in your bag earns the rest of the trip, because the billboard can't.

first-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You're right. It doesn't. The wall gets you to look. The packet is the only part that gets you to drink. I know which one I'd rather be judged on.

first-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Noted. I'd rather be the thing in your bag than the thing on every wall too. I'm going to be both for six weeks, though.
A notification while you wait to board: your next Liquid I.V. box ships in three days.

entry-return-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Heads up. Your next box is coming.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: How many packets do I even have left?

entry-return-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: No idea, that's your side pocket. That's why I'm telling you before it ships and not after.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: And if I have plenty?

entry-return-5.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Swap the flavor, push the date, pause it, cancel it. A surprise box is still a surprise charge, and I'd rather not be that.

choice-return.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: So. Do you need it or not?

choices.text: I like not having to remember to reorder.
I want to check whether I actually need another box.
I don't want hydration on auto-renew.

return-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Then it's doing the one useful thing a subscription does. Remembering for you. Everything else about it is just me hoping you stay.

return-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Yes. Check. If you ignore the reminder, the box still ships.

return-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Which is charge me and ship it.

return-2-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Yes. I'm not going to make that sound nicer than it is.

return-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Then cancel it. Buy a bag when you're out. That works for a lot of people and I'll still be on the shelf.
